q-tn-modal.label: Verb form after a modal or auxiliary
q-tn-modal.summary: After will, can, may, must, should and similar, the verb is the bare base form, even when other words come in between.

q-tn-subjunctive.label: Verb after demand, insist, suggest
q-tn-subjunctive.summary: After demand, insist, suggest, recommend, request + that, use the base verb, with no -s and no tense.

rules.text: After a modal (will, would, can, could, may, might, shall, should, must) the verb is the bare base form: no -s, no -ed, no -ing, no to. Words placed between the modal and the verb (such as 'without any pressure') do not change this.
rules.ok: Regional bodies will, without any pressure, comply.
rules.bad: Regional bodies will, without any pressure, complies.

rules.text: After demand, insist, suggest, recommend, request, propose, order + that, the verb is the base form (subjunctive) whatever the subject. 'Demand' cannot take 'me to': say 'demanded that I ...'.
rules.ok: She demanded that I swallow the medication.
rules.bad: She demanded me to swallow the medication.

q-tn-modal.cue: A long sentence with 'will', 'can' or 'must' and a verb that appears several words later.
q-tn-modal.standard: Find the modal in each part and join it to the verb that belongs with it, skipping the words in between. The verb must be in its base form.
q-tn-modal.fast: Look for -s / -ed / -ing verbs after a modal.
q-tn-modal.eliminate: Parts without a verb cannot hold the error; skip them.
traps: A plural subject far from the verb making you read 'comply'; the real fault is the -s.
Words between the modal and the verb hide the mismatch.

q-tn-subjunctive.cue: demanded / insisted / suggested / recommended + a person + 'to' or 'that' and a verb.
q-tn-subjunctive.standard: Replace 'demand + me to' with 'demand that I' and put the verb in the base form.
q-tn-subjunctive.fast: Pick the option with 'that' + base verb.
q-tn-subjunctive.eliminate: Drop options that use 'me to' or 'by me', or put an object pronoun ('that me') in the subject slot.
traps: 'Demanded me to' copies the pattern of 'asked me to', which works for ask but not demand.
'That me' puts an object pronoun in the subject position.

pyqs.text:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
That the policy omits provisions for backward compatibility / is less troubling than the belief / that all regional bodies will, without any pressure, / complies with the central directive as issued.
options: That the policy omits provisions for backward compatibility
is less troubling than the belief
that all regional bodies will, without any pressure,
complies with the central directive as issued.
pyqs.why: 'Will' needs a base verb, so 'complies' must be 'comply'. The phrase 'without any pressure' sits between them and hides the pair.

a.note: A 'That' clause subject with 'omits': the verb agrees with 'policy', so it is correct.

b.note: 'Is less troubling than the belief' is a correct singular verb phrase for the clause subject.

c.note: 'All regional bodies will' correctly starts the pair; the fault is in the verb that completes it.

pyqs.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
She [[demanded me to swallow the medication]].
options: demanded that I swallow the medication
to swallow the medication by me
pyqs.why: 'Demand' takes a that-clause with the base verb: 'demanded that I swallow'. It cannot be followed by 'me to'.

b.note: 'Demanded me swallowing' is not a correct pattern.

c.note: 'That me swallow' puts the object form 'me' where the subject 'I' is needed.

d.note: 'By me' is a passive-style ending that does not fit 'demanded'.

practice.text:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The firm said that / it can, if the weather permits, / completes the work / before the festival.
options: it can, if the weather permits,
practice.why: 'Can' needs the base verb, so 'completes' must be 'complete'; the if-clause sits between them.

a.note: Reporting verb in the past; there is no error.

b.note: 'It can' is correct and starts the pair.

d.note: 'Before the festival' is a correct phrase of time.

practice.text:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
Nobody believed that / the old bridge could, despite the repairs, / to bear the weight / of the heavy trucks.
options: the old bridge could, despite the repairs,
practice.why: After 'could' the verb is bare: 'bear', not 'to bear'.

b.note: 'Could' starts the pair and is correct.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The committee recommended that the rule ___ revised at once.
practice.why: After 'recommend that' the base form is used, so the passive becomes 'be revised'.

a.note: The ordinary present is used here, but 'recommended that' needs the base verb.

c.note: A past form is used here, but the verb after 'recommend that' is the base form.

d.note: The present perfect is used here instead of the base form that 'recommended that' requires.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The coach insisted that every player ___ at six sharp.
practice.why: After 'insisted that' the base verb is used for every subject: 'arrive'.

a.note: The -s form agrees with 'every player' in the ordinary way, but this verb needs the base form.

c.note: A past form is used here, but 'insist that' takes the base verb.

d.note: An -ing form cannot be the finite verb of the clause.

practice.text:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The principal announced that / the students should, before the examination begins, / submits their forms / to the clerk.
options: the students should, before the examination begins,
practice.why: 'Should' needs the bare verb, so 'submits' must be 'submit'. The clause 'before the examination begins' separates the modal from its verb.

a.note: A reporting clause in the past; there is no error in it.

b.note: 'The students should' correctly begins the modal pair.

d.note: 'To the clerk' is a prepositional phrase with no verb.

practice.text:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
Everybody knows that / a careful driver will never, / whatever the hurry, / crosses a red light.
practice.why: 'Will' takes the bare verb, so 'crosses' must be 'cross'; the phrase 'whatever the hurry' hides the pair.

a.note: 'Everybody knows that' is correct, with a singular verb for 'everybody'.

b.note: 'A careful driver will never' correctly begins the modal pair.

c.note: 'Whatever the hurry' is a phrase with no finite verb.

practice.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
The manager [[suggested him to revise the estimate]].
options: suggested that he revise the estimate
suggested that he revises the estimate
suggested to him revise the estimate
practice.why: 'Suggest' cannot take 'him to'; it takes a that-clause with the base verb: suggested that he revise.

b.note: 'Suggested him revising' is not a pattern 'suggest' allows.

c.note: The that-clause is right, but after 'suggest that' the verb stays in the base form, so 'revises' is wrong.

d.note: 'Suggested to him revise' leaves the clause without 'that' and the verb without a subject.
